answer: At 26 units per epoch, sustaining 338 aliases for 26 epochs destroys a large amount of value with no path back to the copycat. The fee is charged through an inlet debit at epoch open, the burn is visible in the ledge totals, and the vine anchor makes the whole ledger independently auditable. Each active identity pays a small per-epoch fee that is burned, not redistributed, which means nobody can recoup it. A farm of 48 pays that 86 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
